A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LDMI/Hyper-Transformer Decoder work. Their text, equations, figures, Tables 1–5, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and v1's incorrect running header.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, reconstruction, and completion results across image, climate, and shape data, including quantitative comparisons and the decoder ablation in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original quantitative experiments, qualitative generation and reconstruction results, completion examples, and the Appendix C decoder ablation.

M1.justification: Both retain latent tokenization, the Transformer encoder/decoder, grouped weight reconstruction, and the same two training strategies in Algorithms 1–2. Revised notation and clearer compatibility descriptions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 narrows reported completion coverage from structured/unstructured masking and CelebA/ImageNet to structured CelebA-HQ completion. The displayed inpainting cases remain identical, so relabeling them does not establish a dataset substitution. The principal image, ShapeNet Chairs, and ERA5 coverage remains.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GASP, Functa, VAMoH, Spatial Functa, and the MLP decoder comparator with unchanged membership. Changes to Dupont citation suffixes do not change the evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated pretrained configuration from CelebA-HQ 64×64 with LDM-VQ-4 and ImageNet with LDM-VQ-8 to CelebA-HQ 256×256 and ImageNet using LDM-VQ-4. This aligns the prose with the already-existing Table 5 settings; it does not establish rerunning experiments. Numerical training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The completion case study is narrowed by dropping the claimed random-mask and ImageNet tests from Section 4.5, while retaining identical structured face-inpainting examples. Appendix C's parameter-efficiency analysis, MLP-versus-HD ablation, and multiresolution demonstrations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Posterior distributions and multiple conditional samples describe model stochasticity rather than experimental uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–4 are unchanged, including ImageNet FID 6.94 and the decoder-ablation PSNR values 24.93 and 27.72 dB. v1 Figure 4b's ImageNet generations are replaced by CelebA-HQ 256×256 generations in v3 Figure 5b. Section 4.5 also removes the ImageNet completion finding; these changes establish no same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical model, reconstruction operators, variational objectives, and diffusion equations retain their substance. Appendix A.2.1 removes duplicated DDIM equations and explanation, while layer indexing and other notation are refined; no distinct theoretical result or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: probabilistic Transformer-based INR generation, scalable cross-modal modeling, and training either from scratch or by adapting pretrained LDMs. The rewritten conclusion reiterates these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 3.5 and 4.4 explicitly explain compatibility with VAE-, VQ-VAE-, and VQGAN-based LDMs. v3 removes v1's limited-training qualification and expectation of improvement with longer training, and drops the reconstruction caption's interpretation concerning zoomed-out CelebA versus zoomed-in CelebA-HQ.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-reproduction pointer in Section 4.1 and corrects the stated pretrained-model identifiers. Appendix D retains the hardware disclosure and Table 5's numerical architecture, optimization, and training-budget details; labeling VAEs as beta-VAEs clarifies previously documented regularization.

R1.justification: v3 adds Johnson et al. (2016) and Larsen et al. (2016) to the perceptual-loss background. Positioning relative to Functa, Trans-INR, HyperDreamBooth, Neural Diffusion Processes, and Simformer is substantially retained; most other reference changes are bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites and condenses the background, revises the hyper-transforming and completion discussions, reorganizes reconstruction exposition, and rewrites the conclusion. It also fixes broken figure references and the running header, removes duplicated DDIM exposition, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column layout with substantially rearranged figures and tables. Former Figure 2 is split into the I-VAE overview and a separate diffusion schematic, Figure 3 gains token labels, and the generation grid is replaced. Appendix figures are resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility through repaired cross-references, removal of duplicated exposition, clearer diagrams, a code pointer, and pretrained-model descriptions consistent with Table 5. Quantitative evidence remains unchanged. Removing ImageNet generation examples reduces qualitative support, and dataset-label ambiguity persists, limiting the overall gain.
